Issued at 248 AM EST Thu Nov 26 2026

GOES-East Nighttime Microphysics RGB imagery over the Upper Great 
Lakes shows a couple of cloud decks: a scattered high cirrus deck 
and a broken low stratus deck that METAR reports over the southern 
and eastern UP show to be around 2-3kft. The high cirrus deck is not 
expected to have any impact to the weather this morning, but the low 
stratus deck is inhibiting radiational cooling. This is most evident 
in the stark temperature gradient between sites such as Menominee at 
33 degrees as of 05Z and some interior western RAWS sites that are 
reporting single digit temperatures at 05Z. Several different 
model suites show potential for fog formation this morning, and 
while it initially was believed to be a little too dry for this,
webcams at CMX are showing some fog, so some patchy fog has 
been introduced to the forecast.

Aloft, the 500mb pattern shows a deep trough over much of the 
eastern CONUS opposing ridges over the western Atlantic, the High 
Plains, and northern Ontario/Quebec. The latter high has resulted in 
the UP being under the influence of a high pressure that the RAP 
analyzes at 1041mb over Montreal this morning with a surface ridge 
extending over the UP at around 1035mb. This will keep benign 
weather over the UP for Thanksgiving with temperatures around the 
seasonal norms, light winds, and no precipitation. 

The aforementioned deep longwave trough is currently forcing a 
~1001mb low along the Carolinas coast. The GEFS sends this low to 
western New York around 991mb and kicking the high pressure east and 
out of the area. While this low will be too far away to bring 
precipitation to any of the mainland UP, the tightening pressure 
gradient will drive some gusts of 15-25 mph over the east half of 
the UP and over Lake Michigan by Friday. Meanwhile, a 500mb 
shortwave transiting from Alberta to Manitoba from tonight to Friday 
night will instigate a GEFS-mean 993mb low over Lake Winnipeg by 00Z 
Saturday. This will pass a cold front across the UP Friday night 
through Saturday afternoon. This front will have pretty weak forcing 
given the parent low pressure will be approximately 600 miles to the 
northwest, and any showers that do form will be fighting dry air 
(NAEFS PWATs around 0.25"). Despite the factors working against 
precipitation, the LREF does show a 35-55% chance of at least some 
measurable (0.01"+) precipitation falling with the front by 18Z 
Saturday. However, as even 90th percentile precipitation totals are 
less than a tenth of an inch, if precipitation does occur, it will 
be light and not impactful. The NBM tries to resolve some isolated 
freezing rain, but given LREF probabilities of a glaze of ice are 
less than 15%, have removed any freezing rain from this forecast 
package. Accumulating snow is similarly unlikely, though 
thermodynamic profiles do support at least some light snow along 
with rain chances.

As the 500mb trough passes, it will slow over northern Ontario, 
putting the UP in a cold advection regime that will see 850mb 
temperatures fall steadily through the weekend and into the 
beginning of next week. As Lake Superior is currently analyzed to be 
around 6-8C, the first LREF mean 850mb temperatures around the 
threshold of marginal lake enhancement to lake effect precip occurs 
around 00Z Sunday in the west. By Monday morning, all of Lake 
Superior will be under an 850mb airmass that is around -10C, well 
cold enough for lake effect precipitation. Surface temperatures 
throughout the Saturday PM through early next week time period are 
around the freezing mark, so subtle changes in the temperature 
forecast could have significant leverage on the precip type and snow 
ratio forecast (and thus, the snow total forecast). Additionally, 
there is still some spread in modeled solutions on how the trough 
pushes east to Quebec and also in the strength of the trailing 
ridge, both of which will dictate when lake effect precipitation 
ends. Those who will be driving home after the holiday in this 
period may want to keep a close eye on this forecast and consider 
alternate routes in case the lake effect makes some routes 
challenging to drive on. Winds will also be gusty as Euro ensemble 
mean gusts along Lake Superior are in excess of 30 mph by 00Z Mon, 
which if lake effect snow is occurring, could make routes like the 
Seney Stretch of M-28 or M-26 along the Keweenaw difficult to manage 
with low visibility and drifting snow. This is far from a guaranteed 
solution though as the NBM doesn't even have PoPs above 20% for much 
of the Keweenaw Peninsula 00Z Monday as well as gusts of less than 
25 mph on land. All of this to say, uncertainty in the forecast is 
high, which is troublesome given the timing with post-holiday travel.
